statusHistory.note: Raised from a production report of two symptoms: an administrator cannot delete leads, and workspace creation fails. Registered as BUG-006 and BUG-007. The two were deliberately not assumed to share a cause.

BUG-006 reproduced on the exact deployed image (master-suite/web:c879c6c7f7e8): the leads list offers Assign, Change stage, Add task and no delete at all. Every layer below the screen verified working - permission granted at ORGANIZATION scope, route implemented, service soft-deletes, RLS policies and role grants identical to production, cross-tenant delete refused. BUG-007 did not reproduce: the wizard and the API both answer 201 on the same image, and PlatformAuditEvent shows the wizard has worked in production.
R2 path. Six files, no migration, no dependency, no environment change, nothing under lib/auth or lib/security. BUG-007 gets diagnosability, not a speculative fix - it has no reproduced cause.
Artefact set complete for R2: spec, plan, test plan, tasks, traceability, and the two bug records.
Gate 1, author-level, which is what R2 requires. See the approvals entry for the provenance.

Implemented. The compiler found the second LeadGrid caller (sales/smart-views/page.tsx) because the new prop is required rather than optional - an administrator working from a saved view had the same missing control.

Pushed as 21705d7, PR #47 into dev/yourhan-next. GitHub SDD validation: success. CI: every gate passes except Audit, which fails on three advisories published between 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-09 (next critical, nodemailer high, sharp high). This change touches no dependency - git diff 63daf3d..21705d7 over package.json and package-lock.json is empty - and re-running the release candidate's own CI on 2026-09-09 reproduced the identical single failure at 63daf3d with E2E green, so the RC is no longer CI-green either. E2E did not run on this PR because ci.yml gates it on base_ref == main; it runs on the RC PR.

Second pass against the four product requirements. Lead document upload investigated end to end and found already implemented and secure - BUG-010, no defect, coverage added. Task deletion implemented - BUG-009: tasks:DELETE was granted in production, Task.deletedAt existed, every list already filtered it, and the endpoint answered 405. Platform console denial UX fixed for a signed-in non-owner. A bounded 40-check functionality matrix on the production image found exactly two failures, both now closed. One new R4 defect found and deliberately NOT fixed: BUG-008, the console's refusal returns the control-plane page in the redirect body; it reproduces on the unmodified production image, and moving authorization into eleven pages needs the R4 gate.

Full gate green on rc/incident-2026-09-09 at 90ee47a (PR #49, base main so E2E runs): all 34 CI steps pass including E2E, Build and Audit. Playwright 54 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. REG-001 - an administrator deletes a lead from the list - executed and passed at 6.3s. All three workspace-persona assertions passed, and the pre-existing 'a workspace administrator cannot reach the platform area' still passes, so the denial-UX change weakened nothing. REG-002 skips its storage half because CI has no object storage; registered for the R5 owner. Audit is green for the first time since 2026-09-08 via PR #48. BUG-008 remains open at the R4 gate and is deliberately not in this change.

approvals.scope: R2 bugfix: a bulk delete affordance on the leads grid over the existing DELETE endpoint, plus rejection logging and an error message on the workspace provisioning path.
approvals.note: PROVENANCE, stated so it can be weighed rather than assumed. R2's gate 1 is author-level per docs/sdd/RISK_TO_PROCESS_MATRIX.md, but SDD-V022 requires a human on the specification gate at every level, and that refusal is correct. This entry therefore rests on a human instruction given in session on 2026-09-09: 'For R0-R3: continue autonomously according to governance', in a message that named both symptoms as P0 and listed the fix classes that were and were not acceptable. It is a standing class authorization, not a decision taken against this specification document, and an AI agent transcribed it - the same provenance as SPEC-0006. The R2 classification is argued explicitly in spec.md so a reviewer can reject it cheaply; if the R4 reading is taken instead, CHG-001 reverts on its own.
